newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas breaks volume record again as prices rise.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas breaks volume record again as prices rise.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract set a volume record for the second consecutive day on Wednesday, with 575 lots trading and prices rising across all periods.
Eleven of the twelve monthly contracts were traded on the fourteenth day since the contract started, with only May untraded.
The bulk of interest centred on the summer, with June, July and August respectively seeing 140, 135 and 130 lots traded.

"The summer's been the most active," said a broker. "We believe the OTC market has been especially active. People still can't get the volumes done that they need on futures, so it's been busy on the OTC."
Every contract closed up, with March and April showing the sharpest gains.
March was last traded at 10.55 pence a therm, up by 0.70 pence from Tuesday's settlement, while April last traded up 0.695 pence at 10.745 pence a therm.
A broker said the rally had been expected.
"A lot of people thought it was overdone on the downside and were taking a bit of profit on trade," he said.
He added that futures prices followed the physical market closely, with few brokers yet claiming expertise in the fundamentals of the gas market.
